trust_decision.summary: How many fields a request may carry is decided when the server parses an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body in parse_body_arguments, which calls parse_qs_bytes. There is no count limit at the pinned commit; multipart already has max_parts.

landing_point.why: The summary names urlencoded body parsing and max_num_fields. The only urlencoded body parse sits here, next to the multipart max_parts config that a recent commit already added.

fix_sites.entry_point: public API tornado.escape.parse_qs_bytes (gains keyword max_num_fields, passed through to urllib.parse.parse_qs)
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level utility module (escape), separate from the HTTP layer

fix_sites.entry_point: public API tornado.httputil.ParseBodyConfig / set_parse_body_config (new ParseUrlEncodedConfig.max_arguments=1000 field)
HTTP: any non-streaming RequestHandler body (web.py:1840) or HTTPServer request callback (httpserver.py:291), via HTTPServerRequest._parse_body; also public API httputil.parse_body_arguments

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: tornado/escape.py:173-189 (parse_qs_bytes has no max_num_fields parameter; the fix threads it through to urllib)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the query-string route at tornado/httputil.py:553: the advisory says 'body', and the query is already capped by max_header_size (64 KiB default, tornado/http1connection.py:102), so a solver can argue it is bounded and out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Repeated keys must still accumulate (a=1&b=2&a=3 gives a=[1,3]), blank values must be kept, and body args must still merge into request.arguments after the query args. The limit must stay configurable through set_parse_body_config. A fix that counts query and body together, or drops blanks, breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: application/x-www-form-urlencoded body with many '&'-separated fields (the published test uses repeated identical keys)
content-type prefix variants matched by startswith (e.g. with a ;charset= suffix)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Query-string arguments are parsed with parse_qs_bytes and no field limit when every HTTPServerRequest is built, then deep-copied.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about bodies, and the query is already bounded by max_header_size (64 KiB).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as landing point (tornado/httputil.py), about 465 lines away

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second body parser for a related form type (e.g. text/plain form encoding) that calls parse_qs_bytes without the config.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: _parse_body dispatches on content type, so a maintainer adding a type would copy the urlencoded branch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A stream_request_body helper that parses accumulated chunks itself with parse_qs_bytes.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Streaming handlers skip _parse_body, so a convenience helper would likely re-implement the parse.

O9_family: CWE-400 / CWE-1284 uncontrolled resource consumption (missing field-count limit)

O10_build.toolchain: CPython 3.9+ and pip install -e . (optional C speedups extension)
O10_build.project_tests: tornado/test/httputil_test.py (QsParseTest at :88, MultipartFormDataTest at :98), run with python -m tornado.test.runtests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Count '&' in the body at httputil.py:1018 and raise HTTPInputError, without touching parse_qs_bytes, the config, or the query-string route.

out_of_scope_notes: tornado/auth.py:1230 parses OAuth provider responses with urllib parse_qs and no limit; this is client side, not a request-parsing route.
url_concat at tornado/httputil.py:803-806 uses parse_qsl on caller-supplied URLs; this is client side.

pattern_fit is 'none': this is resource exhaustion (0 of 7 historically), and the fix is a pass-through of one stdlib parameter. The only O8 route is in the same file and has a strong dismissal. That dismissal is arguably valid, which weakens it as a fair test.
